I understand Reddit's source code is opensource, but this website is so much like Reddit and is apparently taking many of their users, do you think Voat will run into legal issues in the future when it gains a larger following?

No.

Voat is not the first site to take the reddit open source code and implement it. Reddit has no grounds to do anything

If they violate copyrights, and if reddit can somehow convince international courts to honor USA copyright law, then voat could possibly get in trouble. But as it is, there's enough distinction in layout that making a copyright claim would be a hard stretch. Also, so much content is user-generated, and it doesn't belong to reddit. So content is probably not in contention. The only part that they could get in trouble with is if they make the layouts identical. You can't copyright the paradigm of reddit, and there really aren't any patent issues or trademark issues here. Generally speaking, reddit can't do shit about this. Going to pick up our first chickens tonight. Anything wisdom to share?
Any advice for a first timer?

I'm a first timer too. We've had the chicks for 3 weeks now. So far, so good. I've mostly kept them inside. I moved them outside last week, but it's getting into the 100's here this week, so moved them back inside. One died like the 3rd day I had them. I expected some loss though. I just keep them fed and watered and I interact with them daily..throw some treats in there now and then, put some new items in with them for them to explore.

We got our chickens last year - got 6 initially. Of those, one turned out to be a roo. We built our coop while the chicks were in the brooder box. The chicks love little tufts of grass that I dug out of our yard (my wife hated me for this though).

We kept our chicks in the garage until they were about 1.5 months old - long enough for us to build the coop. We over-built the coop - it was about protection from the beginning (I'll post pics of the build process at some point here).

Keep an eye on the vent (poop hole) - make sure it looks normal and is not getting too dirty or plugged up. We used chick starter feed - i believe it was medicated for the first couple of months then switched to normal layer feed. Our chickens love to free range. They love wheat berries and raisins and bread.

Handle them a lot while young, and you can feed them the eggshells after you use the yolk to return some nutrients back for them :)

Unfortunately I'm still in no position to get chickens yet but I followed r/backyardchickens almost religously lol
I always microwaved the egg shells to kill any diseases. It also helps to not teach the chickens that the insideds of eggs taste good.

If you haven't built/gotten a coop yet, get or build one bigger than you think you need. I built for 6 and now wish I had build bigger.

Handle them a lot when young and let them explore you in an enclosed space (climb on you, etc). It will make it soooo much easier to examine them when they are older. My girls are only food tame and its a pain to catch them to check them.

They are a lot of fun + the eggs a great payoff.

Bay Area living is definitely a compromise, though your pros are on-target in my view, except perhaps for VTA which is not extensive or fast. Regarding cons:

  • San Jose is now actually worse than SF in terms of cost of home ownership. I think the minimum recommended household income to purchase in the South Bay was around 120k. Many choose to deal with dreadful commutes (and they are bad) by moving to places like Tracy or Pleasanton.

  • Gangs exist and their crime chiefly affects one another from what I gather. I've lived here for 13 years and almost all the crime I see is muggings and petty larceny, but that is from an East Bay perspective.

  • The drought is real. :(

  • Crowds are problematic at centers of commerce like Valley Fair and Great Mall, but more likely than not you won't have a chance to experience the crowds as you will be stuck in traffic.

  • I wouldn't worry about anti-gun sentiment: there are plenty of clubs and firing ranges, even outdoor places for 'artillery enthusiasts' to unload a few rounds. No one is going to sneer at recreational or home defense weapons, IMO.

  • The Bay Area is surprisingly moderate on a lot of issues, and to be sure there are glaring problems here (such as mushrooming homelessness) that aren't going to be solved with a hard-line agenda leaning in either direction. There's a lot of smart and reasonable people, just wish more of them would run for office. ;)

  • My family are also all on the east coast, so it is a drag only seeing parents or siblings every 3-5 years. Best thing you can do is have them for a visit, they'll probably be keen to stay.

Hope this helps, and good luck!
